name: Gerlossteinbahn
kurzbeschreibung: Gerlossteinbahn in Hainzenberg opens up a family paradise at 1,643 m: Almpromenade, Almflieger zipline, and the Gerlossteinwand via ferrata.
oeffnungszeiten: Ende Mai bis Mitte Okt täglich 08:30–17:00 Uhr (Halbstundentakt)
beschreibung:
Overview

The Gerlossteinbahn is a tradition-steeped reversible aerial tramway with large cabins located in the municipality of Hainzenberg near Zell am Ziller in the Tyrolean Zillertal. It provides access to the idyllic, family-friendly hiking and recreation area on the Gerlosstein at an elevation of 1,643 meters above sea level. As a sun-drenched part of the Zillertal Arena, the plateau at the foot of the mighty, 2,166-meter-high limestone cliff of the Gerlossteinwand offers a haven of tranquility away from the large tourist crowds—characterized by lush alpine meadows, rustic mountain huts, and sweeping panoramic views of the Zillertal and Tux Alps.

Attractions & Leisure Activities

Over a route length of 2,190 meters, the aerial tramway overcomes an elevation gain of nearly 720 meters, transporting hikers in just about seven minutes from the valley station in Dörfl/Hainzenberg (925 m) up to the alpine plateau. On the mountain, an array of active adventures awaits visitors: for families and nature lovers, the Almpromenade was created—a lovingly designed themed circular trail that explains traditional Zillertal alpine farming, local legends, and natural phenomena at interactive stations, culminating in a wooden viewing grandstand with a telescope station. A spectacular adventure for thrill-seekers is the Almflieger Gerlosstein: a state-of-the-art zipline facility covering 1,438 meters across four sections over alpine pastures; securely strapped in, riders zoom downhill at speeds of up to 50 km/h. Alpine climbers are drawn to the Klettersteig Gerlossteinwand: with 380 meters of vertical gain at difficulty grade C/D, it was the first via ferrata in the Zillertal, ascending steeply through the imposing south face to the summit cross at 2,166 m. In winter, the area transforms into a family ski resort featuring the Zillertal's longest floodlit toboggan run at seven kilometers.

Visit & Getting There

The Gerlossteinbahn operates in the summer season from late May to mid-October daily from 08:30 to 17:00 (departures every half hour, continuously during peak demand). Round-trip ticket prices (2025/2026 season): adults €24.00, children (born 2011–2019) €12.00, small children ride free. Holders of the regional Zillertal Activcard ride for free. The Almflieger requires a separate ticket (including equipment and guide). Arrival by car: Inntal Autobahn A12, exit Wiesing/Zillertal, follow the B169 to Zell am Ziller, then take the B165 (Gerlosstraße) approximately four kilometers uphill to the valley station in Hainzenberg (large free parking lot right at the cable car). By public transit: Zillertalbahn (train or bus) to Zell am Ziller station, then bus line 4094 toward Gerlos/Königsleiten directly to the Hainzenberg Gerlossteinbahn stop.

Tips

Both valley and mountain stations as well as the spacious large cabins are barrier-free accessible; the Almpromenade can be navigated with all-terrain strollers. Stop by Berggasthof Gerlosstein directly at the mountain station or the rustic Arbiskogel-Hütte to sample traditional Zillertaler Krapfen or homemade Kaiserschmarrn on the sun terrace.
